headline: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model under MIT license
body: Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents, under an MIT license. The LongCat team reports 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1, while Meituan lists Claude Opus 5 at 89.1. The self-hosting guide describes a cluster of 194 Huawei Ascend accelerators and gives no guidance for Nvidia GPUs.
note: The MIT license allows commercial use, which could give firms that host models themselves another option, though the self-hosting guide covers Huawei chips and offers no Nvidia guidance.

evidence.text: Meituan releases the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents.
The LongCat team at Chinese food delivery company Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, one week after the model's official unveiling.
LongCat-2.5 is built for agents that work through long, multi-step tasks autonomously, particularly coding.
The weights are available under the MIT license, which allows commercial use, modification, and redistribution.
The LongCat team reports 88.4 points on Terminal Bench v2.1, a benchmark that measures how well agents solve command-line tasks.
Meituan lists Claude Opus 5 at 89.1, GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8, and Deepseek-V4.1-Flash at the top of the table with 90.6.
The self-hosting guide describes a cluster of 194 Huawei Ascend accelerators from the Atlas A2 series.
There's no guidance for Nvidia GPUs.
